title: Acts Chapter 26 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 26 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 26 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 26.

questions.question: In Acts 26, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Agrippa permits Paul to speak for himself
Paul describes his life as a Pharisee
Paul talks about the hope of the promise made to the fathers
questions.correctAnswer: Agrippa permits Paul to speak for himself
questions.explanation: Acts 26:1 states, 'Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself.' This is the earliest event in the chapter.

questions.question: Who does Paul address at the beginning of his defense in Acts 26?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:2 states, 'I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee.'

questions.question: According to Paul in Acts 26, what is Agrippa expert in?
options: All customs and questions among the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: All customs and questions among the Jews
questions.explanation: Acts 26:3 says, 'Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews.'

questions.question: Where did Paul live in his youth according to Acts 26?
options: Among his own nation at Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Among his own nation at Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Acts 26:4 states, 'My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem.'

questions.question: What sect of religion did Paul live as a Pharisee in Acts 26?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:5 states, 'after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.'

questions.question: For what hope does Paul say he is judged in Acts 26?
options: The hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers
The hope of becoming a Roman citizen
The hope of wealth and power
questions.correctAnswer: The hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers
questions.explanation: Acts 26:6 states, 'And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers.'

questions.question: How many tribes hope to come to the promise according to Paul in Acts 26?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:7 says, 'Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come.'

questions.question: What question does Paul raise about God in Acts 26?
options: Why should it be thought incredible that God should raise the dead?
How does God create the world?
Why does God choose some and not others?
questions.correctAnswer: Why should it be thought incredible that God should raise the dead?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:8 states, 'Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?'

questions.question: What did Paul think he ought to do contrary to in Acts 26?
options: The name of Jesus of Nazareth
questions.correctAnswer: The name of Jesus of Nazareth
questions.explanation: Acts 26:9 says, 'I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.'

questions.question: What authority did Paul receive in Jerusalem according to Acts 26?
options: Authority from the chief priests to shut up many of the saints in prison
Authority from the Pharisees to teach
questions.correctAnswer: Authority from the chief priests to shut up many of the saints in prison
questions.explanation: Acts 26:10 states, 'having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.'

questions.question: To what extent did Paul persecute the saints according to Acts 26?
options: Only in synagogues in his hometown
questions.explanation: Acts 26:11 says, 'and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.'

questions.question: Paul asked King Agrippa to hear him patiently because Agrippa is expert in Jewish customs and questions.
questions.explanation: Acts 26:3 states, 'wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently' because Agrippa is expert in all customs and questions among the Jews.

questions.question: Paul says that the twelve tribes serve God day and night and hope for the promise.
questions.explanation: Acts 26:7 states, 'our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come' to the promise.

questions.question: Paul says he was a member of the Sadducees sect before becoming a Pharisee.
questions.explanation: Acts 26:5 states Paul lived as a Pharisee of the most straitest sect, not that he was previously a Sadducee.

questions.question: Paul says he received authority from the Roman governor to imprison the saints.
questions.explanation: Acts 26:10 states Paul received authority from the chief priests, not the Roman governor.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 26 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 26 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Paul see at midday while traveling to Damascus?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:13 states that Paul saw 'a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun.'

questions.question: What does Acts 26:18 promise will happen if someone turns from darkness to light?
options: They will receive forgiveness of sins
They will live a long life
They will be free from all trials
questions.correctAnswer: They will receive forgiveness of sins
questions.explanation: Acts 26:18 mentions that turning from darkness to light results in 'that they may receive forgiveness of sins.'

questions.question: Who spoke to Paul in the Hebrew tongue during his vision?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:15 records that the voice Paul heard was Jesus, who said, 'I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.'

questions.question: What was Paul’s response when he heard the voice asking why he persecuted Him?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:15 shows that Paul asked, 'Who art thou, Lord?' in response to the voice.

questions.question: What did Paul say he was not after receiving the heavenly vision?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:19 states, 'I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision,' indicating Paul's obedience.

questions.question: To whom did God send Paul as a minister and witness?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:17 indicates that Paul was sent to both the people and the Gentiles.

questions.question: What does Acts 26:20 indicate that Paul preached about?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:20 highlights that Paul preached that they should 'repent and turn to God.'

questions.question: What was the reason Paul was caught by the Jews in the temple?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:21 states that the Jews caught Paul in the temple for these causes, implying accusations of blasphemy.

questions.question: What does Acts 26:22 refer to regarding Paul's current state?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:22 mentions that Paul continues 'witnessing both to small and great,' indicating his role as a witness.

questions.question: What does Paul claim about his manner of life in Acts 26:4?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:5 shows that Paul lived 'after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.'

questions.question: What was Paul's main hope as stated in Acts 26:6?
options: The hope of the promise made by God
questions.correctAnswer: The hope of the promise made by God
questions.explanation: Acts 26:6 refers to Paul's standing judged 'for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers.'

questions.question: What does Acts 26:8 question regarding God's power?
options: Why should it be thought incredible that God can heal?
Why should it be thought incredible that God should raise the dead?
Why should it be thought incredible that God can create?
Why should it be thought incredible that God can bless?
questions.correctAnswer: Why should it be thought incredible that God should raise the dead?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:8 directly asks, 'Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?' emphasizing God's power.

questions.question: What is the significance of Paul's statement about being a witness?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:22 indicates that Paul is actively witnessing, which is significant for spreading the Gospel.

questions.question: Did Paul feel guilty about his past actions against Christians?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:12 shows Paul recounting his past with authority, but does not indicate he felt guilty; he was transformed.

questions.question: Is it mentioned that Paul performed miracles during his ministry?
questions.explanation: Acts 26 does not mention Paul performing miracles; it focuses on his testimony and witness.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 26 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 26.

questions.question: What does Paul claim Christ should do according to Acts 26:23?
options: Suffer and rise from the dead
questions.correctAnswer: Suffer and rise from the dead
questions.explanation: Acts 26:23 states that Christ should suffer and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead.

questions.question: What accusation does Festus make against Paul in Acts 26:24?
questions.explanation: In Acts 26:24, Festus exclaims that Paul is beside himself, implying he believes Paul has gone mad due to his extensive learning.

questions.question: How does Paul respond to Festus' accusation in Acts 26:25?
questions.explanation: Paul asserts in Acts 26:25 that he is not mad, but speaks forth the words of truth and soberness.

questions.question: What does Paul claim about King Agrippa's knowledge in Acts 26:26?
options: He knows everything about the law
He is unaware of the prophets
questions.explanation: In Acts 26:26, Paul states that the king knows of these things, indicating that Agrippa is aware of the events surrounding Jesus.

questions.question: What does King Agrippa say to Paul in Acts 26:28?
options: Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian
questions.correctAnswer: Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian
questions.explanation: Agrippa's response in Acts 26:28 indicates that Paul almost convinced him to become a Christian.

questions.question: What does Paul wish for all who hear him in Acts 26:29?
options: To be almost and altogether such as I am
questions.correctAnswer: To be almost and altogether such as I am
questions.explanation: In Acts 26:29, Paul expresses a desire that all who hear him would be like him, except for his bonds.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'sophia' in Acts 26:25 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'sophia' translates to 'wisdom', which is relevant in the context of Paul's reasoning and defense.

questions.question: Which literary device is illustrated in Acts 26:29 where Paul expresses his desire?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:29 demonstrates inclusio as Paul frames his desire within the context of being in bonds and sharing his faith.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of resurrection in Acts 26:23?
questions.explanation: Psalm 16:10 says that God will not abandon His holy one to the grave, echoing the theme of resurrection found in Acts 26:23.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage parallels Paul's testimony in Acts 26:18 about turning from darkness to light?
questions.explanation: John 8:12 declares that Jesus is the light of the world, which parallels the theme of turning from darkness to light in Acts 26:18.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Paul's statement in Acts 26:30?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:30 follows Paul's defense, where he speaks to the king and all present.

questions.question: What does Paul emphasize in Acts 26:22 regarding his message?
options: That he witnesses to small and great
That he has been accused unjustly
questions.correctAnswer: That he witnesses to small and great
questions.explanation: Paul emphasizes in Acts 26:22 that he continues to witness to both small and great, sharing the same message.

questions.question: Paul's defense in Acts 26:6 revolves around what hope?
questions.explanation: In Acts 26:6, Paul stands judged for the hope of the promise made by God, which includes the resurrection.

questions.question: True or False: King Agrippa fully accepts Paul's message in Acts 26.
questions.explanation: Agrippa only responds that Paul almost persuades him to be a Christian, indicating he did not fully accept the message.

questions.question: True or False: Paul claims in Acts 26:27 that Agrippa does not believe the prophets.
questions.explanation: In Acts 26:27, Paul asserts that he knows Agrippa believes the prophets, indicating he does believe.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 26 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 26 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 26:6 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation is based on the hope of the promise made by God to the fathers
Salvation requires strict adherence to Pharisaic law
Salvation is earned by works of righteousness
Salvation is only for the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is based on the hope of the promise made by God to the fathers
questions.explanation: Acts 26:6 states that Paul is judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto the fathers, indicating salvation is rooted in God's promise, not human works.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin does Acts 26:9 teach?
options: Human sin includes active opposition to the name of Jesus of Nazareth
Human sin is limited to ignorance of the law
Human sin is only external behavior, not internal disposition
Human sin cannot affect one’s standing before God
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin includes active opposition to the name of Jesus of Nazareth
questions.explanation: Paul confesses in Acts 26:9 that he thought he ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus, showing active sinful opposition to Christ.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification does Acts 26:20 teach?
options: Sanctification involves repentance and doing works meet for repentance
Sanctification is purely positional and requires no transformation
Sanctification is only for the Jewish people
Sanctification is an instantaneous event without process
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves repentance and doing works meet for repentance
questions.explanation: Acts 26:20 shows Paul preached repentance and doing works meet for repentance, indicating sanctification is both turning and corresponding action.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 26:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Acts 26:8 questions why it should be incredible that God should raise the dead, demonstrating God's omnipotence over life and death.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 26:16 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: In Acts 26:16, Jesus reveals He has appeared for a purpose to appoint Paul as minister and witness, showing divine sovereign election and commissioning.

questions.question: How does Acts 26 connect to the broader redemptive-historical theme of witness and testimony in Scripture?
options: It shows Paul fulfilling the prophetic witness to Christ's resurrection to both Jews and Gentiles
It limits the gospel to Jewish audiences
It focuses only on legal defense without theological implications
questions.correctAnswer: It shows Paul fulfilling the prophetic witness to Christ's resurrection to both Jews and Gentiles
questions.explanation: Acts 26:22-23 highlight Paul's witness to both small and great, confirming Christ’s suffering and resurrection as foretold by prophets, connecting to Old Testament prophecy.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Paul’s appeal to King Agrippa in Acts 26:27-28 emphasize?
options: The fulfillment of prophetic promises is universally accessible, even to rulers
The gospel is only for the common people
Faith is coerced through political pressure
Prophecy is irrelevant in the present age
questions.correctAnswer: The fulfillment of prophetic promises is universally accessible, even to rulers
questions.explanation: Paul’s direct appeal to Agrippa and his acknowledgment of Agrippa’s belief highlights the inclusive nature of the gospel promise, extending to all social strata.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Acts 26:18 and Acts 26:20 teach about salvation and sanctification?
options: Salvation involves forgiveness and inheritance by faith, followed by repentance and works fit for repentance
Salvation is by works alone without faith
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation involves forgiveness and inheritance by faith, followed by repentance and works fit for repentance
questions.explanation: Acts 26:18 speaks of forgiveness and inheritance through faith, while 26:20 emphasizes repentance and works, showing a holistic salvation and sanctification process.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 26:5 and Acts 26:23 teach about the continuity of God's plan?
options: The promises to the Jewish people are fulfilled in Christ’s suffering and resurrection
The Old Testament promises are obsolete
The resurrection was an unexpected innovation
questions.correctAnswer: The promises to the Jewish people are fulfilled in Christ’s suffering and resurrection
questions.explanation: Verse 5 shows Paul’s Pharisaic background grounded in Jewish promise, and verse 23 states Christ’s suffering and resurrection fulfill those prophetic promises.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 26:14 and Acts 26:17 teach about divine revelation and mission?
options: God reveals Himself through Christ’s voice and commissions His servant for a mission to both Jews and Gentiles
Divine revelation is private and exclusive
Mission is limited to Israel only
God’s voice is metaphorical and not literal
questions.correctAnswer: God reveals Himself through Christ’s voice and commissions His servant for a mission to both Jews and Gentiles
questions.explanation: Acts 26:14 recounts the voice of Jesus speaking to Paul, and 26:17 shows the sending of Paul to both Jews and Gentiles, combining revelation and commissioning.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Acts 26:24-25 shows Paul was delusional. What does Acts 26:24-25 actually teach?
options: Paul defends his sanity by affirming he speaks words of truth and soberness
Paul admits to being mentally unstable
Paul ignores the accusations of madness
questions.correctAnswer: Paul defends his sanity by affirming he speaks words of truth and soberness
questions.explanation: Acts 26:25 records Paul’s clear denial of madness, asserting that his words are truthful and sober, countering accusations of insanity.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice and human authority is taught in Acts 26:32?
options: Human authorities must respect divine justice, but appeal to Caesar can override local judgments
Human authorities have absolute finality without appeal
Divine justice is irrelevant in human courts
Caesar’s authority is unlimited and unchallengeable
questions.correctAnswer: Human authorities must respect divine justice, but appeal to Caesar can override local judgments
questions.explanation: Agrippa’s statement in Acts 26:32 indicates Paul could have been freed but appealed to Caesar, showing interplay between divine justice and Roman legal processes.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 26:7 teach about the nature of Israel's hope?
options: The twelve tribes serve God day and night with the hope of the promise
Israel's hope is based solely on political restoration
The hope is uncertain and wavering
questions.correctAnswer: The twelve tribes serve God day and night with the hope of the promise
questions.explanation: Acts 26:7 emphasizes the continual service of the twelve tribes to God, anchored in their hope for the promise.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly highlighted in Acts 26:26 regarding King Agrippa's awareness?
questions.explanation: Paul asserts in Acts 26:26 that the king knows of these things and that none are hidden from him, illustrating God's omniscience communicated through human awareness.

questions.question: What theological significance does Paul’s commission in Acts 26:17-18 have concerning the inclusion of Gentiles?
options: It shows God’s plan explicitly includes turning Gentiles from darkness to light
It restricts salvation to the Jewish people only
It suggests Gentiles are excluded from forgiveness
It implies Gentiles must first become Jews
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God’s plan explicitly includes turning Gentiles from darkness to light
questions.explanation: Acts 26:17-18 highlights Paul being sent to Gentiles to open their eyes and turn them to God, marking the inclusive scope of salvation.
